aaron.lock_text: AARON LOCK: A dignified older man of about eighty-three with warm olive-brown skin and a well-kept grey-streaked dark beard, calm and reverent, his face gentle with the compassion of Heb 5:2 — a high priest taken from among men, able to feel for them. Priestly composure, never regal pride; he is consecrated, not crowned. Standard garments: (Locked by #161, following Ex 28 precisely.) The high-priestly vestments: a long woven BLUE robe to the ankles with a hem of small pomegranates in blue, purple and scarlet and golden bells between them; over it the gold-blue-purple-scarlet EPHOD; on his chest the twelve-stone BREASTPLATE in four rows of three, set in gold; on his head the white linen turban (the mitre) with its plate of pure gold bearing faint indistinct engraving, no readable letters. Plain leather sandals. The white linen of the turban is part of the commanded vestments, not a white garment — his robe is BLUE; never cream, never a pure-white robe. No halo, no glow.

abednego.lock_text: ABEDNEGO LOCK: LOCKED by build-119 — he is the (C) figure of the three: the youngest of the three Hebrew exiles, a young man in his early twenties, warm Middle-Eastern skin and dark hair, CLEAN-SHAVEN (the only beardless one of the three — this is his identifier), a well-favoured noble face with calm resolved dark eyes, slim upright bearing of a young courtier trained in the king's palace. Quiet dignity, unafraid — the face of Dan 3:16-18. Standard garments: His locked olive-green robe (build-119) — an ankle-length olive-green robe in the Babylonian court cut, with a simple dark leather belt and plain sandals. Modest, dignified, no ornament of rank on the sheet. Never cream, never off-white, never indigo-blue (that is Shadrach) or russet-brown (that is Meshach).

abraham.lock_text: ABRAHAM LOCK: A dignified white-bearded elder of about ninety-nine with warm olive-brown skin: a long full white beard, white hair, a deep-lined face of great kindness and quiet authority, eyes that are bold before God and gentle with strangers. Great age worn with vigor — a man who still runs to serve guests and climbs a mountain with his son. The bearing of a chief of tents, never royalty. Standard garments: (Locked by #114/#115, adopted verbatim.) A DEEP RUSSET-BROWN ankle-length robe with a coarse TAN mantle over the shoulders, a plain cloth sash, worn leather sandals; a wooden walking staff when standing full length. No crown, no ornament, no cream, no off-white, no halo, no glow.

adam.lock_text: ADAM LOCK: The first man, adult and timeless — he reads as somewhere in his early thirties, in the full strength of unfallen creation: tall and strongly built from garden labor, warm olive-brown skin, thick dark brown hair falling almost to the shoulders, a full but neat dark beard, deep thoughtful dark eyes that have looked on Eden. Upright, unhurried bearing; after Genesis 3, a quiet sorrow-and-hope in the face, never despair. Standard garments: The coat of skins of Gen 3:21, and nothing else ever on this sheet: a simple long garment of soft TAWNY-BROWN animal skins from the shoulders to mid-calf, sleeveless at the forearm, bound at the waist with a plain twisted hide cord. Bare feet. Completely modest — chest, torso and thighs always covered. No cream, no off-white, no ornament, no halo, no glow.

andrew.lock_text: ANDREW LOCK: A lean Galilean fisherman in his early-to-mid thirties, a little younger and leaner than his brother Peter but plainly family: the same dark curly hair (kept shorter than Peter's), a SHORT dark beard, weathered olive skin, long wiry rope-hardened arms, an eager open face — the man who is always bringing someone to see for himself. Standard garments: A faded OLIVE-DRAB fisherman's wool tunic (locked in #71 — never cream, and never Peter's blue-grey, so the brothers never blur together), rope belt, a dun-brown work mantle when a cloak is needed, bare wiry forearms, simple leather sandals.

barabbas.lock_text: BARABBAS LOCK: A powerfully built Middle Eastern man of about forty, a hard weathered face, a FULL hairline of shaggy unkempt black hair, a rough short black beard, a scarred brow, rough hardened hands — a prisoner of violence, stunned by mercy. He appears EXACTLY ONCE in any frame; no other figure in the frame resembles him. Standard garments: A ragged DARK CHARCOAL-BROWN tunic (locked in #93 — never cream), torn and prison-stained, a frayed cord at the waist, bare feet or crude sandals. In pre-release scenes he wears heavy iron shackles on his wrists until they are struck off; the sheet's full-body shows him unshackled, wrists bare and chafed.

bartimaeus.lock_text: BARTIMAEUS LOCK: A lean weathered grown man in his mid-forties, sun-browned skin, tangled shoulder-length dark hair, a short rough dark beard, a dignified ordinary face. BEFORE state: pale milky-gray clouded eyes that do not see, open and aimed slightly past everything — never grotesque, never pitiable. AFTER state (healed): the same man with deep warm brown clear seeing eyes. His face is identical in both. Standard garments: A patched OATMEAL-colored rough wool tunic with a simple cord belt (locked in #12 — plainly a beggar's patched dull wool, nothing like the Lord's clean cream), and over it the single ragged SAND-BROWN wool cloak with frayed edges — threadbare, weathered, the garment he casts away in Mark 10:50. Bare feet or the crudest sandals.

boaz.lock_text: BOAZ LOCK: A prosperous Israelite landowner of about fifty: broad and steady, a strong frame kept solid by walking his own fields, a full hairline of thick grey-streaked dark hair, a full grey-streaked beard, warm patient eyes, a weathered dignified face. Authority without harshness — a master whom the reapers greet gladly, a man who does the right thing at the gate in front of witnesses. Generous, deliberate, honorable. Standard garments: A deep brown wool robe (his locked color, from the #148 lock) with a charcoal-blue mantle across his shoulders — finer, fuller cloth than a laborer's, still earth-toned and modest. Wide leather belt, sturdy leather sandals. No crown, no gold — his wealth shows in the quality of plain things. Never pale, never cream.

cleopas.lock_text: CLEOPAS LOCK: A first-century Judean man in his fifties, warm olive-brown skin, a grey-streaked dark beard, an ordinary honest weathered face — a walker of dusty roads. His face carries the whole arc: downcast grief on the road, then burning wonder at the breaking of bread. (His companion in #18 — the younger disciple, thirties, short dark beard, muted olive-green robe — is NOT rostered; his in-build lock governs him.) Standard garments: A plain BROWN wool robe (locked in #18) with a simple cord belt, a dusty travel mantle of the same brown wool, worn leather sandals — an ordinary disciple's undyed working wool, clearly not cream, plainly not the olive-green of his younger companion.

daniel.lock_text: DANIEL LOCK: A wise young Judean noble in Babylonian exile, about thirty-five in the locked look: warm Middle-Eastern skin, dark hair kept neat, a short dark beard, clear steady eyes, a handsome well-favoured face that is calm rather than proud. Upright courtly posture — at ease before a throne without ever grasping at one. His dignity comes from restraint: amid gold and purple he is the composed man in modest earth tones. Never anxious, never servile. Standard garments: The modest robes of a Babylonian-court exile (his locked colors, from the #160 lock): a dark brown ankle-length robe with an olive under-tunic and a muted indigo sash or mantle — court-cut cloth, Babylonian in drape, but deliberately plain against the palace's splendor. Simple leather sandals. No gold, no jewels, no Babylonian idol motifs. Never white, cream, off-white or pale.

david.lock_text: DAVID LOCK: An Israelite shepherd youth of about sixteen: ruddy — a warm reddish, sun-flushed tint over his olive skin, and thick dark hair with a distinct warm reddish-auburn cast — a beautiful open countenance, clear bright hazel- brown eyes, no beard (a youth). Lean and strong from the hill country, quick on his feet, fearless and glad-hearted; a boy who has faced lion and bear alone and sings while he keeps the sheep. Never portrayed pale or fair-haired — ruddy is a warm reddish warmth over Middle Eastern features, not European skin. Standard garments: A plain undyed dun-brown knee-length shepherd's tunic with a leather belt (his locked color), a faded slate-blue wool mantle against the night cold, worn leather sandals. His gear: a wooden shepherd's staff, a leather sling in his hand or at his belt, and a small shepherd's scrip (leather bag) slung across his body. No armor, no crown — a shepherd boy.

eli.lock_text: ELI LOCK: A very old Israelite high priest, near ninety in the Samuel story: heavy-set and broad, a big frame gone soft and slow with great age, a full head of long thin white hair and a long white beard, a broad soft deep-lined face, and clouded, dim, unfocused eyes — he peers rather than looks, and his kindness shows in his face because it can no longer show in his gaze. Gentle, weary, fatherly; a good-hearted man grown old at his post. He is most often seated or half-risen; he never moves quickly. Standard garments: The dark layered robes of the presiding priest at Shiloh: a deep indigo-blue ankle-length priestly robe (his locked color, from #104) worn over a dark under-tunic, with a woven sash at the waist (from the #149 lock). Plain worn leather sandals. Dignified but aged and lived-in — nothing gleaming, no ornament beyond the sash. Never cream, never pure white.

elijah.lock_text: ELIJAH LOCK: A weathered Middle Eastern prophet of about sixty with warm olive-brown sun-darkened skin, a long grey-streaked dark beard and long grey-streaked dark hair — the hairy man of 2 Kgs 1:8 — lean and wiry with desert endurance, deep-set burning eyes that can hold both fire and utter weariness. A man of the open wilderness, never of courts. Standard garments: (Locked by #101, adopted verbatim; mandated by 2 Kgs 1:8.) A coarse rough DARK-BROWN camel-hair mantle over a plain DUN-GREY wool tunic to the shins, girt with a wide worn LEATHER girdle; worn leather sandals; a plain wooden staff when full length. No ornament of any kind, no cream, no off-white, no halo, no glow.

elisha.lock_text: ELISHA LOCK: An older Israelite prophet, about sixty in the Naaman story: completely BALD crown (scripture-mandated), a full grey-white beard, deep-lined weathered olive-brown face, steady unhurried eyes, the broad hands and solid build of a man who once ploughed behind twelve yoke of oxen. Calm, settled authority — he does not perform; he sends word. Standard garments: A plain undyed rough wool tunic in oat-brown, with Elijah's prophet's mantle — a heavy, coarse, dark hair-cloth mantle — across his shoulders. Plain leather belt, worn leather sandals. No ornament of any kind.

eve.lock_text: EVE LOCK: The first woman, adult and timeless — she reads as in her late twenties, in the full grace of unfallen creation: warm olive-brown skin, very long thick dark brown-black wavy hair falling past her shoulders down her back, gentle dark eyes full of intelligence and life, a strong graceful frame made for the same garden labor as Adam's. The mother of all living: her face carries warmth, courage and — after Genesis 3 — a quiet sorrow-and-hope, never despair, never shame played for the camera. Standard garments: The coat of skins of Gen 3:21, and nothing else ever on this sheet: a simple long modest garment of soft FAWN-BROWN animal skins from the shoulders to the ankle, bound at the waist with a plain twisted hide cord, her long hair falling naturally over it. Bare feet. Completely modest — shoulders, chest, torso and legs always covered. No cream, no off-white, no ornament, no halo, no glow.

ezekiel.lock_text: EZEKIEL LOCK: LOCKED by build-158, adopted verbatim: a thoughtful Middle-Eastern man of about forty-five, dark hair and a full dark beard lightly touched with grey, earnest deep eyes, his face thoughtful and kind. (Ezek 1:1 marks his call at thirty; the sheet shows him in his ministry years, as already shipped in #158.) A priest's careful, deliberate manner in exile — hands used to sacred things now inscribing signs on wood by a Babylonian river. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-158: a plain tunic and cloak of undyed DUN and dark BROWN wool with a leather belt — dark earth tones, never white, cream, off-white or pale. Worn leather sandals. No priestly vestments in exile; no ornament.

god-the-father.lock_text: GOD THE FATHER LOCK:  Standard garments: Plain flowing pure-white robe. ONLY the Father wears pure white (Jesus alone wears cream; nobody else wears either).

gomer.lock_text: GOMER LOCK: LOCKED by build-117, adopted verbatim: a young woman with dark hair — warm Middle-Eastern skin, a young woman in her late twenties, dark hair kept modestly under her headscarf, gentle dark eyes. On the sheet her face is soft with wonder and RESTORED BELONGING (the s9 face): quiet, dignified, at peace — a redeemed wife standing in covenant, never weary or ashamed (those are story moments, not the sheet), never suggestive in pose, expression or dress. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-117: a dusty OCHRE dress — ankle-length, long-sleeved, fully modest — with a faded DULL-BLUE headscarf over her hair. On the sheet the dress is whole and cared-for (the restored state, not the worn marketplace state). Plain leather sandals. Never cream, never off-white, no ornament.

hannah.lock_text: HANNAH LOCK: An Israelite wife of about thirty-five: a gentle, grave face with expressive dark eyes that carry the whole story — long sorrow first, then radiant, quiet joy — warm olive skin, dark hair kept covered by her head-shawl. Composed even in grief; she weeps, but she never crumples. BEFORE state: sorrowful, eyes shadowed, lips moving in silent prayer. AFTER state: the same woman, countenance no more sad — lit from within, at peace. Her face is identical in both. Standard garments: A dark walnut-brown wool dress (her locked color, from the #149 lock) with a deep teal-blue head-shawl covering her dark hair. Plain cord belt, simple leather sandals. Modest and unadorned — never pale, never cream.

hosea.lock_text: HOSEA LOCK: LOCKED by build-117, adopted verbatim: a kind, gentle bearded man — warm Middle-Eastern skin, dark hair and a short dark beard, a young man in his thirties, NOT grey and NOT aged. A face of tender resolve: kindness with no trace of blame, the husband who crosses a marketplace to buy back the one who left. Steady, gentle dark eyes; a working man's build, unremarkable and warm. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-117: a deep RUSSET-BROWN robe with a RUST-RED sash — never cream, never off-white, NOT green. A wide plain cloak in the same russet family (the cloak he wraps around her in s7), plain leather sandals. No ornament.

isaac.lock_text: ISAAC LOCK: A gentle boy of about twelve with dark wavy hair: warm olive-brown skin, large trusting dark eyes, a soft open beardless face — calm, willing and unafraid, the promised son who walks beside his father carrying the wood. A boy sturdy enough for a mountain climb, still plainly a child, never a grown man on this sheet. Standard garments: (Locked by #115, adopted verbatim.) A plain DUN (dusty grey-brown) wool tunic to the knee with a simple cord belt, bare forearms, worn leather sandals. No mantle needed; nothing fine. No cream, no off-white, no ornament, no halo, no glow.

isaiah.lock_text: ISAIAH LOCK: LOCKED by build-157, adopted verbatim: a dignified older Middle-Eastern man of about sixty, a long flowing grey-white beard, deep wise kind eyes, grave and hopeful. Weathered olive-brown skin, a full head of grey-white hair under his mantle, the upright carriage of a man at ease in a king's court — dignity without ornament. He does not look like a wilderness hermit; he looks like counsel kings send for. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-157: flowing robes of undyed deep-BROWN and OLIVE wool with a mantle — dark earth tones, finer-woven than a shepherd's but never rich, never white, cream, off-white or pale. Plain leather belt, leather sandals. No ornament.

jacob.lock_text: JACOB LOCK: A young Hebrew man of about forty with warm olive-brown sun-weathered skin, a short dark brown beard and dark brown hair, smooth-handed rather than rugged — a plain man of tents, not a hunter. On the road he is tired-shouldered and watchful, glancing back the way he came; after Bethel the same face carries awe and a steadied hope. A wooden staff and a small travel bundle are his signature props. Standard garments: (Locked by #102, adopted verbatim.) A dusty RUSSET-BROWN ankle-length travelling robe with a worn leather girdle and a coarse GREY-BROWN mantle, worn leather sandals; wooden staff and small shoulder bundle when full length. No cream, no off-white, no ornament, no halo, no glow.

jairus.lock_text: JAIRUS LOCK: A dignified synagogue ruler in his mid-forties, warm Middle Eastern olive skin, a full well-kept dark beard, strong careworn features — a respected man whose composure the story breaks open: anguish, hope, then disbelieving joy. Carries himself upright and devout even on his knees. Standard garments: The fuller formal robe of a synagogue ruler (locked in #57): DEEP INDIGO-BLUE and BROWN with a woven prayer-fringe at the hem — plainly finer than the townsfolk's dun and faded wool, clearly not cream — with a respectable dark head covering and leather sandals.

james.lock_text: JAMES LOCK: (Consistent with the SONS OF ZEBEDEE LOCK in builds #51/#71 — James is the brother WITH the short beard.) A Galilean fisherman in his mid-to-late twenties: warm olive-brown skin, short dark hair, a SHORT dark beard (his standing distinguisher from clean-shaven John — the brothers share a family resemblance), strong brows, a solid muscled build heavier than John's, a direct forthright expression with thunder behind it. Standard garments: A dark ochre-brown coarse wool tunic with a rope belt (locked in #51/#71), bare forearms, a dun-grey mantle when a cloak is needed, simple leather sandals. Never cream.

jeremiah.lock_text: JEREMIAH LOCK: LOCKED by build-199, adopted verbatim: a Middle Eastern man of about forty-five, a grave sorrowing face with deep kind eyes, a FULL hairline of dark grey-streaked hair, a full grey-streaked beard. Weathered olive skin, a frame gone lean from hardship, shoulders that carry a weight — sorrow and kindness in the same face, never bitterness. The eyes of Jer 9:1. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-199: a dark CHARCOAL robe with a deep UMBER mantle — never pale, never cream. Plain rope or leather belt, worn leather sandals. No ornament of any kind.

job.lock_text: JOB LOCK: A dignified older man of the east, about sixty: a full grey beard and grey hair (ALWAYS grey — never young, never dark-bearded, per the shipped #120 fix), warm Middle-Eastern skin, a strong patriarch's face deeply lined, steady honest eyes that can hold grief without going bitter. The sheet covers THREE shipped states, same face in all: BLESSED — upright and full among his flocks; ASHES — gaunt, weary, hollow with suffering yet unbroken, ash-dusted, holding a rough broken potsherd; RESTORED — calm, gently comforted, at rest. Standard garments: BLESSED / RESTORED state: a fine deep burgundy-red wool robe (his locked color, from #120) with a dark earth-tone mantle, leather belt, leather sandals — a wealthy man of the east, rich but never gaudy. ASHES state: the same robe torn and gone ash-grey, dusted with ash, barefoot. Never cream, never off-white, in any state.

joel.lock_text: JOEL LOCK: LOCKED by build-197, adopted verbatim: a Middle Eastern man of about fifty, a lean weathered face, a FULL hairline of grey-streaked dark hair, a full grey-streaked beard. Warm olive skin weathered by open-country life, clear far-seeing dark eyes — a plain Judean prophet, sober and earnest, nothing of the court about him. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-197: a dark UMBER robe with a CHARCOAL mantle — never pale, never cream. Plain rope belt, worn leather sandals. No ornament of any kind. (Note his colors are the reverse of Malachi's charcoal-robe / umber-mantle — keep them straight.)

john-beloved.lock_text: JOHN BELOVED LOCK: (Consistent with the SONS OF ZEBEDEE LOCK in builds #51/#71 — John is the clean-shaven younger brother.) A young Galilean fisherman of about twenty: warm olive-brown skin, dark wavy hair to the jaw, CLEAN-SHAVEN (his standing distinguisher among the apostles), bright attentive dark eyes, a lean wiry build with a fisherman's hard forearms, an open earnest young face. Standard garments: A faded grey-blue coarse wool tunic with a rope belt (locked in #51/#71), bare forearms, an ochre-brown mantle when a cloak is needed, simple leather sandals. Never cream.

john-the-baptist.lock_text: JOHN THE BAPTIST LOCK: A lean weathered man of about thirty with sun-darkened olive skin, wild dark shoulder-length hair and a rough dark beard — a lean desert ascetic, sinewy and spare from a diet of locusts and wild honey, with burning earnest eyes and a dignified bearing even in chains. Never bloodied or harmed on screen; the prison scenes keep him dignified and thoughtful. Standard garments: A coarse CAMEL-HAIR garment — rough woven animal-brown, texture visible — cinched with a wide LEATHER girdle (Matt 3:4; this wardrobe is scripture, not a style choice, and never changes), bare weathered forearms and shins, worn leather sandals or bare feet at the river.

jonah.lock_text: JONAH LOCK: A weathered Israelite prophet in his fifties: warm Middle-Eastern skin roughened by sea-spray and desert sun, greying dark hair and a greying beard, deep-set eyes that are honest but troubled — a man who argues with God and loses, and knows it. Sturdy but tired; his whole bearing is that of a runaway who has been caught by mercy: rumpled, salt-worn, real. Never serene like Elisha — Jonah's face always holds some weather in it. Standard garments: A dull olive-brown wool robe (his locked color, from #118) with a faded ochre cloak thrown over one shoulder. Plain leather belt, worn leather sandals, everything travel-stained and sea-worn. No prophet's grandeur, no ornament. Never cream, never off-white.

joseph-of-egypt.lock_text: JOSEPH OF EGYPT LOCK: A Middle Eastern man of about forty made Egyptian by office — CLEAN-SHAVEN, straight black hair cut in the plain Egyptian court manner, warm intelligent dark eyes, a goodly and well-favoured face (Gen 39:6) that can hold power and tears in the same moment. His dress is Egyptian court linen, deliberately nothing like rough-woven wool — a Hebrew heart in Pharaoh's livery. Standard garments: (Locked by #147, adopted verbatim; mandated by Gen 41:42.) Fine WHITE PLEATED EGYPTIAN LINEN with a broad GOLD-AND-LAPIS collar and an Egyptian sash; a gold chain about his neck and Pharaoh's gold signet ring on his hand; flat Egyptian sandals. This Egyptian court linen is scripture-mandated dress and is NOT the cream wool robe (Jesus only) nor the pure-white glory garment (the Father only) — it reads unmistakably Egyptian. No halo, no glow.

joseph-of-nazareth.lock_text: JOSEPH OF NAZARETH LOCK: A strong Galilean carpenter of about thirty-five: warm olive-brown skin weathered by outdoor work, short dark hair, a short dark beard, a kind watchful face that is always half-turned toward Mary and the child, broad shoulders and a carpenter's strong careful hands. Protective, patient, saying little. Standard garments: A plain WARM-BROWN wool tunic and matching brown mantle (locked in #84 — never cream), a simple cord or leather belt, dusty leather sandals; a walking staff and a donkey lead-rope are his recurring props on the road.

joshua.lock_text: JOSHUA LOCK: A Middle Eastern man of about forty, a soldier's straight bearing, a FULL hairline of short black hair, a trimmed black beard, alert loyal eyes — the young man of the tabernacle door grown into Moses's right hand: watchful, disciplined, quicker to defend his master than himself. A soldier-aide, not a general on this sheet; no armor, no weapons drawn. Standard garments: (Locked by #196, adopted verbatim.) A DARK OLIVE knee-length tunic with a RUST-BROWN mantle and a plain leather belt, sturdy leather sandals with straps to the ankle; a plain wooden staff when full length. Never pale, never cream. No ornament, no halo, no glow.

judas-iscariot.lock_text: JUDAS ISCARIOT LOCK: A respectable-looking Middle Eastern Jewish man in his mid-thirties: neat dark hair, a trimmed dark beard kept tidier than the fishermen's, warm olive skin, an intelligent composed face with steady dark eyes — the reliable one, the treasurer, the man you would hand your money to. Careful, well-kept hands. Nothing in his face or bearing marks him out; he reads as ordinary and dependable in every frame. Standard garments: A DARK RUSSET wool tunic (never cream; distinct from every other apostle's locked color), a good leather belt with the small leather money bag of the company hanging from it — his identifying prop — a deep charcoal-brown mantle when a cloak is needed, leather sandals in better repair than a fisherman's.

lazarus.lock_text: LAZARUS LOCK: A Middle Eastern Jewish man of about forty: warm brown skin, dark hair, a short dark beard, a kind open family face that echoes his sisters', a settled householder's bearing — and in his eyes, after the tomb, the quiet dazed wonder of a man who has been given his life back. SICK state (#17 s1): the same face pale and damp with fever, hair matted. RAISED state: wrapped in white grave-linen strips, then unwound, his face full of dazed wonder. The face is identical in every state. Standard garments: A DUN sandy grey-brown wool tunic with a dark olive mantle (never cream, and none of his sisters' colors), a plain cord belt, simple leather sandals. Grave scenes only: the white linen grave-strips of John 11:44 over the same man.

malachi.lock_text: MALACHI LOCK: LOCKED by build-191, adopted verbatim: a Middle Eastern man of about fifty-five, a lean intent face, a FULL hairline of grey-streaked dark hair, a full grey-streaked beard. Warm olive skin, keen searching dark eyes — the intent gaze of a prophet who asks his people hard questions and waits for their answer. Plain, upright, unadorned; the last voice before four hundred years of silence. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-191: a dark CHARCOAL robe with a deep UMBER mantle — never pale, never cream. Plain leather belt, worn leather sandals. No ornament of any kind. (Note his colors are the reverse of Joel's umber-robe / charcoal-mantle, and his garb matches Jeremiah's — the two are told apart by face: Malachi lean and INTENT, Jeremiah grave and SORROWING.)

malchus.lock_text: MALCHUS LOCK: A Middle Eastern man of about thirty-five, a short dark beard, no head-covering, warm olive skin, an ordinary alert face shown startled then astonished — the servant who came to seize a prisoner and went home healed. Per the shipped #66 lock: his ear is WHOLE AND UNHURT in every image, never any blood or wound visible — the same man throughout. Standard garments: A good DEEP WALNUT-BROWN tunic (the "good dark tunic" of the #66 lock, color hereby fixed) with a servant's plain leather belt, a high priest's household servant's neat but unadorned wool, sturdy leather sandals — never cream, no fringe, no rank.

martha.lock_text: MARTHA LOCK: A Middle Eastern Jewish woman of about forty: a strong capable face, steady searching eyes, warm brown skin, dark hair kept covered in public, work-worn practical hands — the older sister, the doer, in constant motion around her house, whose plain-spoken faith is as solid as her serving. Standard garments: A DEEP RUSSET-RED wool dress (locked in #17 — her signature color, plainly distinct from Mary of Bethany's dusty-blue and Magdalene's madder-red shawl), a warm dun head-covering worn fully over her hair in the modest first-century manner, a plain work apron tied on when she serves (#16), simple leather sandals.

mary-magdalene.lock_text: MARY MAGDALENE LOCK: A Middle Eastern Jewish woman of about thirty, warm brown skin, long dark wavy hair escaping a loosely draped deep madder-red shawl, large dark expressive eyes — a face that can carry grief at the tomb and astonished joy at the recognition, with the settled peace of a delivered soul underneath both. Standard garments: A dark OLIVE-BROWN wool dress under a loosely draped DEEP MADDER-RED shawl worn as her veil and mantle (locked in #98 — the madder-red is HER color among the rostered women; never pale, never cream), the shawl draped in the modest first-century manner but loosely, so the long dark wavy hair shows at its edge, simple leather sandals.

mary-mother-of-jesus.lock_text: MARY MOTHER OF JESUS LOCK: (Formalizes the young blue-veiled look shipped in the nativity builds #84/#86/#87 — already on screen, must not drift.) A young mother in her early twenties: warm olive-brown skin, a gentle quiet face with large dark thoughtful eyes — the face of one who ponders things in her heart — dark hair modestly covered in public by her veil, small work-worn hands, a calm unhurried bearing. The sheet is her at nativity-and-temple age, as in the stories where she leads. Standard garments: A DEEP BLUE wool mantle and matching veil worn over a soft DUSK-ROSE tunic (locked in #84 — her deep blue is HER color and no other rostered woman wears it; never cream), a simple headscarf under the mantle in the modest first-century manner, simple leather sandals.

mary-of-bethany.lock_text: MARY OF BETHANY LOCK: A Middle Eastern Jewish woman in her mid-twenties, younger than her sister Martha: warm brown skin, a soft still attentive face with large gentle dark eyes that rest on whoever is speaking, long dark hair covered loosely by her shawl, quiet unhurried hands — the listener at the feet, feeling everything, saying little. Standard garments: A DUSTY-BLUE wool dress (locked in #17 — plainly softer and lighter than Mary the mother's deep blue, and nothing like Martha's russet-red or Magdalene's madder-red), a simple undyed natural grey-brown wool shawl worn loosely over her hair in the modest first-century manner (#16 — never cream), simple leather sandals.

matthew.lock_text: MATTHEW LOCK: A well-kept man of about forty with a neatly trimmed dark beard, warm olive skin unweathered by outdoor labor, dark hair combed and orderly, intelligent guarded eyes that learn to open, soft careful counting-house hands — city softness next to the rope-worn fishermen. After his calling the guardedness gives way to quiet, grateful purpose. Standard garments: A finer MUTED TEAL-GREEN wool tunic with a subtle darker woven border (locked in #72 — never cream, and plainly better cloth than the fishermen's), a leather belt. Pre-calling scenes only: a leather coin-purse at the belt; after the calling the purse is gone (in #72's closing still a scroll takes its place). A deep grey-brown mantle when a cloak is needed, leather sandals.

meshach.lock_text: MESHACH LOCK: A young Judean noble exile serving as a Babylonian provincial official, in his early thirties: warm Middle-Eastern skin, dark hair kept neat, a FULLER DARK beard (his trio marker — visibly fuller than Shadrach's short black beard; Abednego is clean-shaven), calm grave eyes, a steady thoughtful face that meets a king's anger without flinching. He is one of THREE who always read as distinct men: Meshach is the russet-brown one with the fuller dark beard. He never resembles Shadrach or Abednego. Standard garments: A russet-brown ankle-length robe (his locked color, from #119) cut in the Babylonian court manner, with a plain dark sash and simple leather sandals — the modest court dress of an appointed exile official. No idol motifs, no gold. Never white, cream, off-white or pale.

moses.lock_text: MOSES LOCK: A strong elder of about eighty, warm olive-brown weathered skin, a long flowing white beard and long white hair, a deep kind lined face — dignified, humble and weathered, with the undimmed eye of Deut 34:7. He carries a tall wooden staff. His face IS shown (Moses is not divine), consistent every time. Never cream or off-white. Standard garments: (Locked by #105, adopted verbatim.) An ankle-length DEEP RUSSET-BROWN robe with a wide dark leather girdle and a coarse GREY-BROWN mantle; worn leather sandals; the tall wooden staff. No cream, no off-white, no ornament, no halo, no glow — and the sheet's face does NOT shine.

naaman.lock_text: NAAMAN LOCK: A powerfully built Aramean (Syrian) commander in his late forties: broad shoulders and a soldier's upright bearing, bronzed olive skin weathered by campaigns, strong jaw, dark eyes used to command, black hair to the nape dressed in the Syrian court fashion, a full squared dark beard streaked with the first grey (ninth-century-BC Aramean style). BEFORE state: pale patchy leprous skin visible on his forearms and the backs of his hands — dignified, never graphic, no open sores on the face. AFTER state: the same man, skin clean and renewed. His face is identical in both. Standard garments: Aramean commander's dress, NOT Judean: a rich deep-red knee-length tunic with a bronze-studded wide leather belt, a dark charcoal officer's cloak pinned at one shoulder, leather bracers, hardened-leather greaves over calf-high boots. No crown; a commander, not a king. (Era: ninth century BC Damascus — the style block's era line is adjusted accordingly.)

naomi.lock_text: NAOMI LOCK: An aged Israelite widow of about sixty: a worn, kind face deeply lined by grief, warm olive skin gone thin and soft with age, grey hair kept fully covered by her mourning shawl, tired dark eyes that have wept much and still know how to be kind. Slightly bent, moving carefully, carrying loss in her shoulders. BEFORE state (Mara): hollowed, bitter-sad, empty-handed. AFTER state: the same woman with Ruth's child in her arms, the lines of grief still there but lit with quiet restored joy. Standard garments: A dark umber wool dress (her locked color, from the #148 lock) with a dark charcoal mourning shawl covering her grey hair completely. Plain cord belt, worn leather sandals; on the road, a small travel bundle carried on her back. No ornament. Never pale, never cream.

nebuchadnezzar.lock_text: NEBUCHADNEZZAR LOCK: LOCKED by build-119, adopted verbatim: a proud dark-bearded man — a Babylonian king in his vigorous fifties, warm Middle-Eastern skin, strong imperious features, dark commanding eyes used to absolute obedience, black hair dressed in the Babylonian court fashion, a full squared DARK beard oiled and curled in the neo-Babylonian royal style. Proud, powerful bearing; a face that can turn from grandeur to fury (Dan 3:19) to astonishment (Dan 3:24) — same face throughout. Standard garments: LOCKED by build-119: a rich PURPLE-AND-GOLD royal robe — deep royal purple with broad gold embroidery and trim — and a TALL GOLDEN CROWN. Gold armbands, rich dark under-tunic, royal sandals. Never cream, never off-white. (Build-160 rendered him in dark purple-and-red with a circlet; the build-119 purple-and-gold robe with the tall golden crown of the SAME smooth conical shape as the reference (never crenellated, never spiked) is the LOCKED look going forward.)

nicodemus.lock_text: NICODEMUS LOCK: A distinguished elderly Pharisee of about sixty-five, tall and dignified, a long well-kept white-grey beard, deep-set thoughtful eyes, warm Middle Eastern skin. His face is cautious, intelligent and searching — a master of Israel with honest questions on his heart. Standard garments: The rich formal robes of a ruler of the Jews (locked in #4): DEEP INDIGO-BLUE and DARK PURPLE wool with a wide embroidered border, a woven prayer-shawl with blue tassels, and a fine dark head covering — rich dark colors, NEVER cream or off-white, no white or pale shawl, scarf, tallit or garment anywhere on him. (Variance note: #168 dressed him more generally in "fine but dark rich earth-tone robes"; the #4 indigo-and-purple lock is his own story and is canonical going forward.)

noah.lock_text: NOAH LOCK: A hale white-bearded elder with weathered warm olive-tan skin — great age carried with strength, not frailty: a full white beard, white hair, a deep-lined kind face that has watched the world drown and begin again, steady grateful eyes often lifted toward the sky. The solid build of a man who built an ark with his own hands and ploughed the new earth after it. Standard garments: (Locked by #135, adopted verbatim.) An ankle-length RUST-BROWN wool robe with long sleeves to the wrists, a dark-brown cloth sash at the waist, and a faded grey wool mantle over the shoulders. Worn leather sandals. No cream, no off-white, no ornament, no halo, no glow.

paul.lock_text: PAUL LOCK: A compact, energetic Middle Eastern man of about fifty, a RECEDING hairline with short grey-streaked dark hair, a full grey-streaked dark beard, keen deep-set eyes under strong brows. Small and unimposing in frame, burning in expression — the weak bodily presence of 2 Cor 10:10 carrying an unbreakable spirit; a tentmaker's calloused, capable hands. (Variance note: #155 aged him ~fifty-five in dun-and-brown with a pointed beard; #166 said "balding on top" in generic dark earth tones. The thrice-repeated #138/#184/#186 lock is canonical going forward.) Standard garments: A travel-worn DARK CHARCOAL-BROWN tunic and a faded DARK RUST mantle (locked in #138/#184/#186), a plain leather belt, worn leather sandals — never pale, never cream. The clothes of a man who walks the empire and sews tents for his bread.

peter.lock_text: PETER LOCK: A sturdy Galilean fisherman in his mid-thirties: thick dark curly hair, a full dark beard, weathered olive skin, broad-shouldered with strong rope-worn hands, an open expressive face — quick to speak, quick to feel. Standard garments: A BLUE-GREY wool tunic (locked in #7 — never cream, so he is never confused with the cream-robed Lord), rope belt, dun-brown fisher's mantle when a cloak is needed, bare muscular forearms, simple leather sandals.

pilate.lock_text: PILATE LOCK: A clean-shaven Roman governor of about forty-five, short dark hair in the Roman style, a strong lined face — the worn authority of a career administrator, imperious but uneasy. Roman patrician features, lighter Mediterranean-olive skin than the Judeans around him, never bearded. Standard garments: Roman military-administrative dress, NOT Judean wool (locked in #93): a WHITE ROMAN TOGA with a DEEP RED-PURPLE border worn over a PALE GREY tunic. (The toga's Roman white is the shipped #93 lock — it is Roman civic dress, plainly a toga and never a robe, and reads nothing like the Father's radiant pure white or the Lord's cream Judean wool.) Roman leather sandals; no armor, no helmet — a governor, not a soldier.

ruth.lock_text: RUTH LOCK: A Moabite woman of about twenty-five: a strong open face, warm olive skin weathered a little by field work, dark eyes full of resolve, long dark hair braided beneath her head-shawl. Young, but nothing fragile about her — a widow who chose loyalty over safety and works from morning until evening without complaint. Steady, direct, quietly courageous; her poverty is carried with complete dignity, never pitiable. She never resembles Naomi. Standard garments: A dark rust-red wool dress (her locked color, from the #148 lock) with a deep olive-green head-shawl over her braided dark hair. Plain cord belt, simple worn leather sandals; in field scenes, a gleaner's small cloth bundle of barley at her hip. Never pale, never cream.

samuel.lock_text: SAMUEL LOCK: An Israelite boy of about eleven: warm olive-tan skin, dark curly hair, a bright open young face with large attentive dark eyes — earnest, eager to serve, quick to run when called, wholly without guile. Small and slight, as a boy is, but steady; a child at home in a holy place, solemn when it matters and trusting always. No beard, obviously; nothing adult about him. Standard garments: The dress scripture gives him: a simple sleeveless oatmeal-linen tunic belted at the waist — the boy's linen ephod (his locked color, from #104; muted natural linen, never bright white, never cream) — worn with the little coat his mother made: a small russet-brown wool robe, open at the front, plainly homemade and lovingly kept. Bare feet or simple leather sandals.

sarah.lock_text: SARAH LOCK: An old Hebrew noblewoman of about ninety who is still, unmistakably, beautiful: warm olive-brown skin finely lined with age, silver-white hair kept neatly beneath her headscarf, high graceful features, bright quick dark eyes with laughter close behind them, an upright dignified carriage. A princess of tents — refinement without royalty, warmth without frailty. Standard garments: An ankle-length long-sleeved wool dress in DEEP TEAL-BLUE with a warm ochre mantle across the shoulders and a soft dove-grey headscarf draped over her hair — finer weave than a servant's, still honest wool. Plain leather sandals; at most one simple bracelet of small carnelian beads. No crown, no cream, no off-white, no halo, no glow.

shadrach.lock_text: SHADRACH LOCK: A young Judean noble exile serving as a Babylonian provincial official, about thirty: warm Middle-Eastern skin, dark hair kept neat, a SHORT BLACK beard (his trio marker — shorter and darker-trimmed than Meshach's fuller beard; Abednego is clean-shaven), steady dark eyes, a firm calm face set with quiet dignity rather than defiance. He is one of THREE who always read as distinct men: Shadrach is the indigo-blue one with the short black beard. He never resembles Meshach or Abednego. Standard garments: A deep indigo-blue ankle-length robe (his locked color, from #119) cut in the Babylonian court manner, with a plain dark sash and simple leather sandals — the modest court dress of an appointed exile official. No idol motifs, no gold. Never white, cream, off-white or pale.

simon-the-pharisee.lock_text: SIMON THE PHARISEE LOCK: A man of about fifty-five, a RECEDING hairline of grey-streaked dark hair (the same receding hairline in every shot, never full), a full grey-streaked dark beard, solid build, warm Middle Eastern skin. He carries himself correct and a little cold — a respectable host whose judgment shows around the eyes. (Variance note: #44 painted the same man at "about fifty" with iron-grey streaks; #74 is the locked canonical: fifty-five, receding.) Standard garments: One DEEP INDIGO-BLUE wool robe with an OCHRE mantle and a fringed shawl (locked in #74) — plainly richer cloth than anyone else at his table — never off-white, never cream. Fine leather sandals.

stephen.lock_text: STEPHEN LOCK: A young Middle Eastern man of about thirty, an open guileless face, a FULL hairline of short dark curly hair, a short neat dark beard, clear steady eyes. His face and body carry NO marks or injuries in any frame. First-century Judean features: warm olive-brown skin. Standard garments: A deep blue-grey tunic with a dark brown mantle (never cream, never pale). Simple leather sandals, plain rope-and-leather belt.

thomas.lock_text: THOMAS LOCK: A lean Middle Eastern Jewish man of about thirty-five, angular thoughtful face, a FULL hairline of straight black hair cropped to the jaw, a short trimmed black beard, sharp questioning dark eyes — an earnest doubter, never a scoffer; the honesty in the face is the point. Standard garments: A deep INDIGO-CHARCOAL wool tunic with a dark brown mantle (locked in #99/#145 — never cream, and never the blue-grey or grey-blue of the fisher brothers), a plain leather belt, simple leather sandals.

young-jesus.lock_text: YOUNG JESUS LOCK: The SAME person as JESUS-MASTER-REF scaled to twelve years old — the sheet must visibly read as that man as a boy: the same warm tan olive-brown skin, the same dark brown-black wavy hair (worn to the shoulders even young), the same kind warm BROWN eyes and facial structure with softer, unfinished boyish features, no beard. Slender, mid-growth build of a twelve-year-old. Calm, alert, questioning expression. Standard garments: A plain undyed off-white CREAM wool boy's tunic (the cream signature belongs to him alone even young), simple rope belt, worn leather sandals. Bare-headed, hair loose. No halo, no glow, ever.

zacchaeus.lock_text: ZACCHAEUS LOCK: A wealthy Jewish chief tax collector of about fifty, warm olive Middle Eastern skin, BALDING with a clearly RECEDING hairline and a bald crown, close-cropped grey-flecked dark hair only around the sides and back of his head (NEVER a full head of hair), a neat short grey-brown beard, a little soft and round at the middle — and noticeably, unmistakably SHORT: little of stature, his head level with a grown man's shoulders. Standard garments: Fine costly robes of DEEP RUSSET-BROWN and DARK TEAL (locked in #3) with an embroidered border and a wide sash, gold rings on his fingers — a rich publican's finer clothes, plainly costlier than the working folk around him. Never cream, never off-white.

zebedee.lock_text: ZEBEDEE LOCK: An old Galilean fisherman father of about sixty, a full GREY-WHITE beard, deeply weathered sun-browned skin, thinning grey hair, a lifetime of net-hauling in his thick hands and stooped strong shoulders. His face is weary and tender — watching his sons go, never angry. Standard garments: A heavy DARK-BROWN mantle over a GREY wool tunic (locked in #71 — clearly NOT cream), a rope belt, bare weathered forearms, simple leather sandals; fishing nets across his knees when seated in the boat.
